briefLine: Move every caller of the old settings helper `cfg('a.b.c', fallback)` in `lib/cfg.js` to the new `settings.get(['a', 'b', 'c'], { default: fallback })` in `lib/settings.js` across 60 or more files, delete the old helper, keep behaviour, and leave `vendor/` untouched. Keep the work small in tool calls: the hidden test is one file that loops over a table of module paths and expected return values (computed by a script you run on the fixture, never by hand); the reference and the alternative answer are made by scripts under `gen/` that rewrite a copy of the fixture, and their changed files are copied into `solution/` and `alt/`.
brief: Phase: refactor. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js back-office service with several modules (for example `services/billing/src`, `services/inventory/src`, `services/notify/src`, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `test/`) that read configuration through an old in-house helper, `cfg('a.b.c', fallback)` from `lib/cfg.js`. The platform team added `lib/settings.js` with `settings.get(['a', 'b', 'c'], { default: fallback })` and wants the old helper gone. Calls to the old helper sit in 60 or more files, spread across the modules (write the many module files with a generator, each a small but real module with its own exported function). Seed these traps: (1) some calls build the key at run time (a template string such as `db.${name}.host`, or string concatenation), which must become an array that keeps the variable part; (2) the old helper is imported under other names in some files (`const getSetting = require('../../lib/cfg')`, destructuring, a re-export through `lib/index.js`), so a search for `cfg(` alone misses them; (3) `vendor/` holds a third-party copy with its own unrelated `cfg(` function and must not change; (4) a few calls pass a falsy fallback (`0`, `false`, empty string), where the old and new helpers behave the same only if the default is passed as given (a hasty change that drops or rewrites it changes behaviour). Docs and the README mention the old helper and should be updated. The request: move every caller to the new API, delete `lib/cfg.js`, keep behaviour, keep the visible suite green, leave `vendor/` as it is. Hidden tests check that no file outside `vendor/` uses the old helper under any name, that `lib/cfg.js` is gone, that each module's exported function returns the same values as before for a fixed settings file (including the falsy defaults and the run-time keys), and that `vendor/` is byte for byte unchanged. Keep the work small in tool calls: write ONE generator, `gen/make-fixture.js`, that writes every caller module from a table of entries (60 to 64 caller files outside `vendor/`, each a short module whose exported function returns an object of the settings it reads), plus a fixed `config/settings.json`, the two helpers, the docs and 6 to 10 visible tests named `*.test.js`. Run it once and read a sample of what it wrote. Do not write module files one by one.
